claims.text: Introducing a sintering-aid additive can reduce the temperature required for sintering relative to a pure material.
A suitable sintering aid lowers the activation energy for grain-boundary diffusion.
Lower grain-boundary diffusion activation energy enhances diffusion kinetics at grain boundaries.
A small amount of nanoscale TiO2 or a similar compound can serve as an appropriate dopant or sintering aid.
The dopant segregates to grain boundaries during processing or sintering.
Dopant segregation at grain boundaries reduces the activation energy for diffusion.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion promotes densification at lower temperatures.
The doped material can achieve densification comparable to conventional high-temperature sintering at a lower overall sintering temperature.
The doped material can achieve microstructural properties comparable to conventional high-temperature sintering at a lower temperature.
The effectiveness of the sintering aid depends on the identity and concentration of the dopant.
Formation of unwanted secondary phases may reduce the effectiveness of the additive.
Failure of the additive to segregate uniformly to grain boundaries may reduce its effectiveness.
